- When sentiment is consistently low or neutral, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak.
- If sentiment shows early positive signals (e.g., >0.2), model should adjust downward to reflect market cooling; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- If sentiment remains flat or negative for 3+ days, model should not assume continuation of upward trend; forecast should trend downward or plateau.
- Overshoots after spikes are common in early forecast windows; apply “lag correction” by subtracting 0.5–1.0% from forecast for days 1–5 post-spike.
